subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact phoenix model in a flight pose, deciding how to position it so the lowest point of the wings or tail just touches the ground while keeping the body elevated and dynamic.

I'm sketching out the skeleton structure: hips as the root joint, then a spine chain curving up into the chest, followed by a neck chain leading to the head, each defined with specific 3D coordinates to shape the posture naturally.

For the tail, I'm planning a downward-backward chain of joints, then adding feathers as flat ribbon-shaped sweeps fanned out from the tail base, colored with gold-to-red gradient bands to give a flame-like look, with the center feathers longest and ends tapering near the ground.

For wings, I'm building shoulder-elbow-wrist arm chains spread outward and slightly upward, with primary feathers fanned from the wrist and secondary feathers rooted along the arm between elbow and wrist, each feather a tapered flat ribbon with varying angle and length to create a natural fanned wing shape.

Writing the gradient paint function...

Defining alternating feather gradients...

Now I'm thinking about adding an anime-style eye decal on the head sphere, like Genshin's eye designs—picking iris colors like golden-yellow or phoenix orange, and positioning it on the skull surface with mirroring for symmetry, scaled appropriately for the head size.

Now I'm planning the beak structure using cones for the upper and lower mandibles, attached via a jaw joint to the head, and the neck chain connecting through to the head joint with proper aim direction and parenting to the spine.

Still designing the head and body details...

Now I'm working out the leg geometry: hip, knee, and ankle joints chained together with bend directions, calculating segment lengths to make sure the thigh-shin-foot chain reaches the target foot position properly.

Then I'm adding toes—three forward and one back, built as small cone spikes projecting from the foot point.

Tweaking the toe target height to sit just above the floor. Now I'm thinking about adding flame-like decorative touches—small glowing flame cards placed at the wing tips and tail ends, oriented upright and flickering, to give the creature a fiery accent.

I'm also considering a glowing emblem decal on the chest, like a phoenix sigil, placed by raycasting against the body surface to find the right spot and orientation for it.

Working out the body's spine geometry — rump-to-neck curve and varying radii along the chain — so the sweep shape tapers naturally from rump to chest to neck.

For the neck itself I'll do a separate sweep slightly overlapping the body, then add decorative crest plumes: five ribbon shapes rising from the head crown as a flame-like mane, skipping the more complex ruff-spike idea in favor of something simpler. Now I need to pin down the actual joint coordinates, starting with the hips.

Mapping the spine as a catmull curve through three points rising from the hips up and forward, giving two joints, then continuing that same curve pattern into the neck with another three-point path leading up to where the head will sit, parented off the top spine joint. I'll place the head's parts using absolute coordinates for simplicity rather than fiddling with local bone offsets.

Now I'm figuring out the head sphere's radius and scale, checking proportions against wingspan, and planning the eye decals as mirrored surface details plus a cone-shaped upper beak angled forward and down from the skull's center.

Positioning the beak and jaw cones with their colors, then starting to plan the crest ribbons extending from the head.

Still refining feather geometry...

Now I'm working out the wing geometry per side, defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist points swept upward and outward, then building a three-point polyline chain parented to the spine joint with named shoulder/elbow/wrist joints for the wing role.

I'm sweeping the arm profile with a reddish paint color for the feather covering, then placing nine secondary feathers along the arm polyline at increasing parameter values, computing each root point along the curve and projecting a tip backward and slightly drooping with a varying length curve.

Assigning each feather to the nearest skeletal joint depending on its position, then generating ten primary feathers fanning out from the wrist at increasing angles with decreasing lengths so the outer feather reads as longest.

Checking the wingspan against the body size—scaling down joint positions and feather lengths so a 1.3m body gets a proportionate ~4-5m span rather than something oversized. Now adding covert feathers in warm gold as two shorter, wider rows layered along the arm above the ribbon feathers.

Counting feathers per wing (roughly 34, doubled for both wings) to keep triangle counts manageable, and switching the feather geometry to a flat box section with flat caps instead of rounded tips, since that's cheaper to render and still looks fine given the tapering width.

Now I'm setting up the tail structure — a backward chain of points from the hips forming the tail base, then spawning nine tail feathers radiating from a root point with varying angles and lengths, tapering symmetrically outward from the center.

I'm planning quadratic bezier curves for each feather with a lifted midpoint for arc, varying widths, and a gold-to-orange-to-crimson color gradient, plus small glow accents at the tips. I'm also sketching a layered SVG flame texture for decoration at the tail joints.

Adding card-based flame meshes at tail tips, wing primary tips, and the crest, collected into a frame list during feather generation, then applying a glow pass to those meshes. I'm also considering adding leg feather "trousers" near the hips using orange ellipsoid shapes.

Now I'm placing a chest plume of five gold ribbons hanging from the chest area down and forward, anchored near the neck base and attached to the last spine joint, skipping the full neck ruff idea in favor of this simpler draping effect.

For orientation, I'm setting the up vector to [0,0,1] for the mostly-vertical feather tangents so the ribbon width shows properly from the front, applying this both to the chest plumes and the crest ribbons that sweep up and back.

Finally I'm planning a glowing chest emblem decal — a flame sigil inside a gold circle.

I'm defining the color palette for the feather paints (gold, amber, red, crimson) and setting up a gradient-based paint function that works with the cel-shading system, then starting on a helper to build multi-color feather gradients.

Setting up body paint with countershading for a layered red-orange-to-cream look, flat colors for legs, and establishing the hip joint as root for the tail and spine chains. Now I'm starting the actual builder code with the necessary imports.

Writing imports and vector helper...

Building the wing arm chains and sweeping them, then adding smaller secondary feather-like bones branching off along each arm's path...

Adding covert feather rows and primary coverts now, with slight vertical offsets between layers to avoid z-fighting when drawing back layers before overlapping coverts.

Now I'm moving to legs: positioning hip and foot targets, verifying the distance fits within the limb's reach, and building the limb chain with named joints for the leg sweep and toe placement at the foot.

For toes, I'm computing tip positions by offsetting from the foot with a spread angle, creating flat capsule toes resting near ground level, then adding small dark claw spikes angled outward from each toe tip.

Now I'm adding a thigh puff using a scaled sphere at the hip joint for body shape, then moving to build the head: creating a neck-to-head joint and attaching a skull sphere scaled to a slightly flattened oval shape.

Next I'm placing eye decals by raycasting around the skull surface to find attachment points and normals, then planning the beak as a simple cone and adding neck ruff plumes as a ring of ribbon feathers radiating down and outward from the neck base, mirroring the earlier chest plume approach.

Now I'm working on the emblem sigil placement, computing a surface ray hit near the chest to position a gold circle-and-flame decal, then defining the body sweep radius profile and adding a tail base sweep.

Continuing with the tail chain curve and a flame texture made of layered SVG paths (outer red, mid orange, inner yellow flame shapes scaled and nested), then applying it as card frames oriented upward along the tail with crossed geometry.

Now I'm figuring out the crest spikes along the top, placing root and tip points for each spine so they curve backward and upward with varying height based on distance from center, then adding a flame accent at the middle tip.

Adding cheek tufts...
